_comment: Proposed furniture layout for the example apartment. Metres, plan coordinates. size = [width, depth, height]; the item's FRONT is its local +Y side (the side you sit on / open / face), rotated counter-clockwise by rotation_deg (0 = front faces plan +Y, -90 = faces +X, 90 = faces -X, 180 = faces -Y). Types with clearance rules: sofa, armchair, bed, dining_table, desk, wardrobe, sideboard, bookcase, tv_unit, kitchen_run. Rugs never block. 'asset' is optional: the .blend/.glb to place instead of a proxy. tv_unit takes 'screen_in' (diagonal, inches); 'powered': true/false overrides the socket-reach check. The bedside tables here are > 1.5 m from the only bedroom socket, so the checker warns: in a real job that goes to the client as a decision (extension lead, move, or new socket as electrical work). Decor types (never block walking routes): curtain (width, depth = fold depth, height = rod height), wall_art ('elevation' = bottom edge), cushion ('elevation' = seat height, optional 'material'), pendant ('elevation' = shade bottom; hang it on a ceiling outlet from the dossier). Optional top-level 'palette': {material name: [r, g, b]} restyles the stand-in furniture (see PALETTE in furnish.py).
